# Exact optimization region for dominated midpoint sandwich centers

This note characterizes all centers obtainable by optimizing a dominated
midpoint submeasure. It gives a finite-dimensional support dual and a
precise obstruction to repairing the known selector by this optimization.
It does not prove OC.

Let A,K,C be positive-volume convex bodies in R^d, d>=1, with
(A+C)/2 subset K. Write a=|A|, b=|K|, c=|C|, and let g_K be the
ordinary centroid of K. Put the three bodies at integer indices -1,0,1.

A permitted coupling is a finite nonnegative measure pi on A x C whose
marginals sigma_A,sigma_C are dominated by their respective uniform
volume measures. Its two marginal masses are the same number t. Write
eta for its midpoint pushforward. In this note also require eta<=1_K dx.
The associated sandwich center is

    g(pi)=[b g_K+2 integral x d eta]/(b+2t).            (1)

Zero coupling, t=0, is permitted. It gives g_K.

## 1. The density constraint imposes no extra first-moment restriction

For every pair of endpoint submeasures sigma_A<=1_A dx,
sigma_C<=1_C dx of the same mass t>0, there EXISTS a coupling with
those exact marginals whose midpoint measure satisfies eta<=dx.
Its support lies in (A+C)/2, so eta<=1_K dx.

Here is the proof for arbitrary dominated submeasures, rather than just
uniform subsets. Normalize their densities to probability densities,
both bounded by 1/t. Smooth both by a centered Gaussian. The triangular
transport from the first smoothed density f to the second g has positive
diagonal derivatives and determinant f/(g composed with T). Its
midpoint map F=(Id+T)/2 has determinant at least sqrt(det DT), by the
diagonal arithmetic-geometric mean inequality. The midpoint probability
density is therefore at most sqrt(f(x)g(T(x)))<=1/t.

The smoothed marginal families are tight. A weak limit of their joint
couplings retains the two prescribed original marginals. The midpoint
map is continuous, and testing against nonnegative compactly supported
continuous functions passes the density bound to the limit. Multiplying
by t gives eta<=dx. This is the same proved triangular construction
as in `candidate 71bcdfc8eb8340c6`, and
does not require the submeasure densities to be indicators or log-concave.

Every midpoint coupling, regardless of density, has the first moment

    2 integral x d eta=integral x d sigma_A+integral x d sigma_C.   (2)

Thus the construction proves that imposing eta<=1_K changes no feasible
first moments once the two endpoint submeasures are specified.

## 2. The exact compact convex set of attainable centers

For a body E and 0<t<=|E| define its trimmed-centroid body

    Z_t(E)={t^(-1) integral x d sigma:
                    0<=sigma<=1_E dx, sigma(E)=t}.

This is compact and convex: the admissible submeasures form a weakly
compact convex set on compact E, and their moment map is continuous
and linear. For fixed t, (1)-(2) give the EXACT attainable center set

    Y_t=[b g_K+t Z_t(A)+t Z_t(C)]/(b+2t).              (3)

The inclusion from a coupling to (3) follows from its marginals, and
the reverse inclusion follows from Section 1. The complete center set is

    Y={g_K} union union_(0<t<=min(a,c)) Y_t.           (4)

The permitted coupling family is weakly compact: it is a closed family
of finite measures on compact A x C, of uniformly bounded mass, with
closed marginal domination and closed midpoint domination constraints.
Its center map has denominator at least b>0 and is continuous. Thus Y
is compact.

It is also convex, despite the varying denominators in (3). If two
couplings have masses t_1,t_2 and centers y_1,y_2, put M_i=b+2t_i.
For any 0<=lambda<=1 choose

    theta=lambda M_2/[(1-lambda)M_1+lambda M_2].

The permitted coupling theta pi_1+(1-theta)pi_2 has center exactly
lambda y_1+(1-lambda)y_2. Every point of Y belongs to K because it is
the centroid of a measure supported there and dominating uniform K.

Optimizing a coupling's correlations alone cannot move this center;
only its endpoint submeasure moments and its mass matter. Equations
(3)-(4) incorporate all of those choices, not merely full-mass or
uniform-fraction endpoint choices.

## 3. A two-scalar support dual with attained minimizers

Fix u!=0 in R^d and a real number h. Define

    J_u(h,v)=integral_A (u.x-h+v)_+ dx
               +integral_C (u.x-h-v)_+ dx,
    D_u(h)=b(u.g_K-h)+min_(v in R) J_u(h,v).           (5)

Then the support function h_Y(u)=max_(y in Y)u.y is the UNIQUE root

    D_u(h_Y(u))=0.                                    (6)

Thus the optimization over all coupling measures has an exact support
description using one scalar root and one scalar convex minimization.
The variable v is an equality-of-source-mass multiplier, not an
unproved rounding or shadow parameter.

### Exact duality for the inner minimum

For fixed h, the function J_u(h,v) is convex and continuously
differentiable. Nonzero u makes the affine threshold hyperplanes have
zero volume, so differentiation under the integral gives

    partial_v J_u(h,v)
       =|A intersect {u.x>h-v}|-|C intersect {u.x>h+v}|.            (7)

It is coercive: as v tends to positive infinity the first term grows
at least linearly with slope a, and as v tends to negative infinity
the second grows at least linearly with slope c. Therefore its minimum
is attained at some finite v, where the two selected cap masses in
(7) agree. Take sigma_A,sigma_C to be volume restricted to those two
caps. Their common mass t lies in [0,min(a,c)]. Zero or full caps are
allowed, and weak versus strict thresholds makes no volume difference.

For any other equal-mass dominated submeasures, adding v to one
integrand and subtracting it from the other changes no integral. Each
resulting integral is bounded by the corresponding positive-part
integral over its full body. At a minimizing v, the two cap submeasures
attain both bounds simultaneously. Consequently

    min_v J_u(h,v)
       =max_{sigma_A,sigma_C dominated, equal mass t}
           [integral (u.x-h)d sigma_A
                         +integral (u.x-h)d sigma_C].              (8)

No strong-duality theorem or existence assumption is hidden here:
the balancing derivative directly constructs a primal maximizer.

### The outer root and its support interpretation

By (1)-(2) and Section 1, equation (8) gives

    D_u(h)=max_(permitted pi) (b+2t)[u.g(pi)-h].        (9)

For h_2>h_1, every expression on the right decreases by at least
b(h_2-h_1). Hence D_u is strictly decreasing. It is continuous because
the permitted family is compact and all its masses are bounded.
It tends to negative infinity as h tends to positive infinity, since
Y is compact; it tends to positive infinity as h tends to negative
infinity, already by using the zero coupling. It therefore has one
root. At h=max_Y u.y all expressions in (9) are nonpositive, and a
support maximizer gives zero. This proves (6).

The case u=0 simply has support value zero and requires no threshold
differentiation. The center set itself is full finite-dimensional data;
it does not depend on a selected finite list of cap directions.

The minimum in (5) is taken AFTER forming the positive-part integrals.
It is not exchanged with an integral of optimized tail probabilities.
In particular it is a different object from the previously obstructed
directional capacity-law mean.

## 4. The exact source cap budget survives, but the known example excludes Y

For every closed ambient halfspace H, a midpoint in H requires at
least one of its two source points to be in H. Therefore every
permitted coupling satisfies

    eta(H_0)<=sigma_A(H_-1)+sigma_C(H_1),
    |K intersect H_0|+eta(H_0)<=mu(H),                 (10)

where mu is the original three-fiber mixed volume. This includes all
oblique normals and closed boundary mass. The measure rho in (1)
has twice the eta coefficient, so (10) does NOT identify rho(H_0)
with a source-budget lower bound. The fixed-mass constant with objective
s+2r cannot be substituted for the actual source cost s+r.

Optimizing all of Y still fails on the exact body proved in
`candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`. To state the
certificate precisely, that body has d=5, middle standard simplex K,
and endpoint simplices A=(2-q)D, C=qD, with

    (A+C)/2=D subset K,
    |A|/|K|=a in (0,10^(-5)), |C|/|K|=1,
    q<2, r=497/3000, R=9/2,
    x_1<=r, R x_1+x_2>=(R+1)/6 on D.

Here D is the explicit simplex and a,q are the exact algebraic
parameters defined and certified in that file. For ANY permitted
coupling, its midpoint measure is supported in D. Hence (1) gives

    Y subset conv({g_K} union D).                     (11)

This includes every t, every pair of trimmed endpoint submeasures, and
every midpoint coupling satisfying the density constraint.

The two exact closed ambient caps

    H_1={x_1+(1-q)r z>=1/6-(2/25)a},
    H_2={x_2-2z>=1/6+(17/50)a}

cover the entire right side of (11), as the wedge calculation in that
file proves. Their respective relative masses are

    gamma_5[1+(12/125)a]^5,
    gamma_5[1-(51/125)a]^5+a,

both strictly less than gamma_5(1+a/2) by the displayed exact rational
inequalities there. Thus every point produced by the present optimized
dominated-coupling scheme has original depth strictly below gamma_5/2.
All endpoint points fail the same target as proved in that certificate.

This extends the selector quantification to arbitrary BOTH-endpoint
trimming and all masses t; it does not rely on one endpoint marginal
being its entire uniform measure. It still does not contradict OC:
the body has other available middle-fiber points, including the
separately certified all-halfspace escape point.

## 5. Scope beyond three fibers

The entire two-source characterization works verbatim for any two
actual fibers at indices z_-,z_+ in Z^n whose midpoint m is integer,
using the actual midpoint fiber as K. Other original fibers only add
nonnegative source cap mass to (10). This is a local extension to
arbitrary n and to bodies with any number of fibers.

There is also a direct finite-group extension. Take k positive-volume
source bodies A_j at integer indices whose arithmetic mean is the
integer m, and let K be the actual m-fiber. Equal-mass source
submeasures of mass t admit an average coupling dominated by dx:
smooth their normalized densities, each bounded by 1/t, map a common
reference density to them by triangular maps T_j, and average those
maps. Diagonal arithmetic-geometric mean gives

    det D[(T_1+...+T_k)/k] >= product_j(det DT_j)^(1/k),

so its probability density is at most 1/t. The same compact limiting
argument gives the required average measure eta<=1_K dx.

For rho=1_K+k eta, the center numerator is b g_K plus the sum of
the k source moments. Its support dual replaces (5) by

    b(u.g_K-h)+min_{v_1+...+v_k=0}
                       sum_j integral_(A_j)(u.x-h+v_j)_+ dx.

This convex minimum is attained: on the zero-sum multiplier space,
unbounded multipliers force at least one positive multiplier to tend
to infinity, and its positive-volume source integral diverges. Its
first-order conditions make all k selected cap masses equal, proving
duality exactly as in Section 3. The source indicator budget still
controls only one eta copy, not k copies.

This extension concerns ONE fixed group. Simultaneously reusing source
fibers in several groups requires additional allocation constraints;
adding several output densities in an already occupied midpoint fiber
can violate domination. No iteration, global partition, or preserved
OC constant across those operations is asserted.
